summary.intent: Ship GSD phase 73 (shared-write navigation correctness) fully autonomously through the standard post-execute-phase pipeline: verify, secure, crypto/privacy review, security review, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit CLI review, PR creation, and PR review resolution.
summary.outcome: Phase 73 shipped as PR #603 with all gates green (verify, secure 17/17, crypto/privacy, security-review, Nyquist validation, 106/106 SDK E2E), three real bugs fixed (stale write-access refresh, stale WRITE-04 test contract, seq-consistency guard on refreshSharedFolder), 2 todos logged and 2 false positives correctly rebutted during PR review triage; PR was merged into main and fast-forwarded successfully.

repo: The local dev stack has a TEE-worker host-port collision: `TEE_WORKER_URL` defaults to `http://localhost:3001`, but `cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing` already claims host :3001, pushing the real tee-worker container to host :3002 — causes silent 404s and an empty `tee_key_state` table.

tee-worker `/public-key` endpoint is gated by `Authorization: Bearer $TEE_WORKER_SECRET` (apps/tee-worker/src/middleware/auth.ts) — the host-run API must also be given a matching TEE_WORKER_SECRET or pubkey fetch 401s and tee_key_state never seeds.
`tee_key_state` is populated by the API's TeeKeyStateService fetching the worker's pubkey at boot, not by the worker itself.

Phase 73 commit subjects were already conventional (`fix(73-08):`, `test(73-01):`) — the filter-branch reword step in the ship-phase runbook isn't always necessary; only non-versioned chore/docs commits had parens.

`.planning/todos/pending/2026-07-06-68.2-coderabbit-hardening-backlog.md` is the running hardening backlog for shared-nav/write-key issues — dedupe new findings into it rather than creating new todo files.
CodeRabbit's PR-level review commonly includes hallucinated cross-references to nonexistent phase numbers in `.planning/` doc nits — treat as noise, discard.

code.finding: refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey originally reseeded publishedNode from cached getSharedFolderState() instead of re-resolving via IPNS, so 'Refresh access' could never recover a co-writer stuck on stale-not-revoked state; fixed by mirroring the restoreToBreadcrumbIndex pattern (seed then refreshSharedFolder).

restoreToBreadcrumbIndex's slice(0, crumbIndex) removes the target entry from the write-key stack before its buffer is transferred to currentWriteKeyRef at line 564, giving sole ownership — Greptile's writeKey-aliasing claim (twice) was a false positive; navigateToSubfolder also nulls the source buffer immediately after pushing (transfer-and-null), preventing use-after-free/aliasing.

publishedParent resolve added in phase 73 uses raw resolvePublishedNode without the ROT-07 gate applied to sibling reads; mitigated by seq-monotonicity guard + server CAS, judged non-blocking LOW and logged as a defense-in-depth todo rather than fixed.

refreshSharedFolder adopted children/seq from one resolve but publishedNode from another with no consistency check, risking seeding an older envelope than the adopted children; fixed with a seq-consistency guard mirroring doReresolveFolderInPlace (commit 6c1d6817b).

Test 20 (WRITE-04) asserted the old throw-on-410 contract for createAndPublishIpnsRecord, but phase 73 changed it to catch 410 and return {success:false, tombstoned:true}; updated the test to the new return-value contract after confirming no production caller relied on the old throw.

workflow: Running independent gate checks (secure/crypto/security/validate agents, SDK E2E, CodeRabbit CLI) as parallel background tasks let the ship-phase pipeline proceed without idle waiting.

Piping a long-running test command's exit code through another command can mask the real exit status (`exit code 0` reported but actual run had failures) — check actual output, not just the piped exit code.
When an E2E suite fails, isolate whether failures are infra-config issues vs code regressions by cross-checking against what the phase diff actually touched before spending fix effort.

For PR review threads flagging the same code area across CLI and PR-level passes (or re-raised after a fix), tracing the actual buffer/object lifecycle in code beats trusting the reviewer's suggested fix — a suggested clone-without-zero fix was shown to introduce a real security regression (unzeroed key leak).
Dedupe new review findings into an existing todo backlog file (by appending/editing an item) rather than creating new todo files, to keep the pending todos directory from sprawling.

friction: SDK E2E gate initially failed 3/106 due to local-only TEE-worker stack misconfiguration (port collision + missing auth secret) unrelated to the phase, requiring a lengthy root-cause detour (container status, DB inspection, auth header tracing) before confirming it wasn't a regression.

A backgrounded bash command reported exit code 0 in the task-notification summary while the actual run had exit code 1 with 3 failing tests — the notification/exit-code surfacing was misleading and required manually re-checking output.
`gh pr checks`/API calls hit a transient network timeout requiring a retry.
CodeRabbit's PR-level review included hallucinated references to nonexistent phase numbers in doc nits, adding noise to triage.
